change: No changes. Primary (Lats/LatissimusDorsi, mid back/Rhomboids+LowerTraps, biceps/BicepsBrachii) and secondary (shoulders/PosteriorDeltoid, forearms/WristFlexors, Lats/RotatorCuff) are correct for a prone bench reverse-grip barbell row. Underhand grip justifies biceps as co-primary; WristFlexors correct for supinated grip; LowerTraps+Rhomboids correct prime movers.

Moved Upper Traps from primary mid back to a separate secondary mid back entry. Neutral grip prone rows primarily engage Latissimus Dorsi, Rhomboids, and Lower Traps as prime movers; Upper Traps are stabilizers/secondary during scapular control. Split mid back into two entries: primary [Rhomboids, Lower Traps], secondary [Upper Traps].

Changed forearms latin from WristFlexors to WristExtensors. Pronated (overhand) grip positions wrists so the extensor muscles resist the load during the pull; WristExtensors is the correct encoding for overhand-grip rowing. All other muscles unchanged — Upper Traps justified in primary for pronated grip which shifts emphasis toward upper back.

No changes. Supinated (underhand) grip correctly elevates biceps to co-primary. WristFlexors correct for supinated grip. LowerTraps+Rhomboids as primary mid back and RotatorCuff/PosteriorDeltoid secondary are all well-supported by research.

Removed abs (Upper Rectus Abdominis, LowerRectus Abdominis) from secondary — core engagement is minimal when torso is fully chest-supported on bench, making abs inclusion inflated. Added Lateral Deltoids to secondary shoulders (EMG studies confirm medial/lateral delt secondary activation in front raises). Added chest/Clavicular Head to secondary (EMG and multiple sources confirm pectoralis major clavicular head assists in shoulder flexion during front raises). Expanded mid back secondary from [LowerTraps, Rhomboids] to [Upper Traps, Lower Traps, Rhomboids] — Upper Traps are active scapular stabilizers in overhead/front raise movements.
